title: User Profile Management
stories: As a user, I want to view my profile details so that I can confirm my information is correct.
As a user, I want to edit my profile details so that I can keep my information up to date.
As a user, I want to delete my account so that I can remove my data when I no longer need the service.
As a user, I want to change my password so that I can maintain account security.
note: Clean CRUD decomposition — each story is independent, testable, and maps to one capability.

title: Notification Preferences
stories: As a user, I want to enable or disable a notification channel so that I only receive alerts through channels I prefer.
As a user, I want to set the notification frequency so that I am not overwhelmed by too many messages.
As a user, I want to preview a sample notification so that I know what to expect before enabling a channel.
note: Good separation of concerns — configuration, tuning, and preview are each a distinct user goal.

title: Data Export
stories: As a user, I want to request an export of my data so that I can keep a personal backup.
As a user, I want to choose an export format (CSV, JSON, PDF) so that I can use the data in my preferred tool.
As a user, I want to receive a download link by email so that I can retrieve the export when it is ready.
note: Covers initiation, configuration, and delivery — each independently testable.

title: Search and Filter
stories: As a user, I want to search records by keyword so that I can quickly find what I need.
As a user, I want to filter results by date range so that I can narrow down to a specific period.
As a user, I want to sort results by relevance or date so that the most useful records appear first.
As a user, I want to save a search filter as a preset so that I can reuse it without re-entering criteria.
note: Each story adds one distinct search capability; none depends on the others to be useful.

title: Report Generation
stories: As a manager, I want to select a report template so that the output matches our standard format.
As a manager, I want to specify a date range for the report so that I get data for the relevant period.
As a manager, I want to download the generated report as a PDF so that I can share it offline.
note: Template selection, parameterisation, and output are separate concerns with clear acceptance criteria.

title: User Onboarding Flow
stories: As a new user, I want to complete a guided setup wizard so that I can configure my workspace without reading documentation.
As a new user, I want to skip optional setup steps so that I can start using the system immediately.
As a new user, I want to see contextual tooltips on my first visit so that I understand key features.
note: Progressive disclosure — each story is a self-contained onboarding capability.

title: Role-Based Access Control
stories: As an admin, I want to create a new role with specific permissions so that I can control what each team can access.
As an admin, I want to assign a role to a user so that their access matches their responsibilities.
As an admin, I want to view an audit log of role changes so that I can track who modified permissions.
note: Admin-facing — role definition, assignment, and auditability are independent capabilities.

title: Student Feedback Collection
stories: As a student, I want to rate a lecture on a 1-5 scale so that I can give quick feedback.
As a student, I want to add a written comment to my rating so that I can explain what worked or did not.
As an instructor, I want to view aggregated feedback per lecture so that I can identify areas to improve.
note: Separates input (rating, comment) from consumption (instructor view) — different actors, different goals.
